exposure: Group B streptococcus (GBS) colonization status in women with late PPROM undergoing expectant management
cohort: The study included singleton pregnancies complicated by late prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM) between 34(+0) and 36(+6) weeks, with documented GBS rectovaginal culture results, who underwent expectant management until 37(+0) weeks.
finding: Expectant management of GBS-colonized women with late PPROM, when accompanied by appropriate antibiotic prophylaxis and close maternal-fetal surveillance, is not significantly associated with adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes and appears to be a safe option.
gest_age: PPROM occurred between 34(+0) and 36(+6) weeks, with expectant management continued until 37(+0) weeks.
